output.name: Ireth
output.myth:
Ireth went north in the spring and south in the autumn, and never once asked anyone's leave. She flew from the ice at the pole to the warm grass of the south and back, more sea than one bird should carry. Aun, the First Flier, asked her how far the wind went. She said, "Further than you. I've been. Get out of my way."

Mother Hesk counts the birds on her Reel every night, and every night Ireth is one short. The village sings for her and hangs her cloth on the cliff. Out to the east, Nethe sits on her black rock, waiting for the sun to dry her before she flies home.

Some grey morning, when the cloth is nearly rotted, Ireth comes in low over the rocks, soaked, cross about the fog, and asks who has been eating her fish. Vanu the Thief-Bird, on the south-west wind, only grins. Tavo laughs and blows her in. Nobody scolds her. Mend the net, the grandmothers say, and set out another bowl.

The lost are not always dead. Some are only slow.
output.finding: Find the Drying Shag, then look a little under a hand-span to her west, and you will find Ireth.
